assertions.name: deuteron_wall_resummation_wrong_transform
assertions.source: classical Gamma-Borel divisor diverges on the q-Gevrey substrate object (q0^{n^2/2}/Gamma(n/2+1)->inf, n<=40) while the q-Borel divisor q0^{n^2/2} tames it; the full-transseries negative resummed the q=1 shadow with the classical transform, so it does not close the substrate deuteron resummation. Mis-scope; no fit.

description: The deuteron-wall resummation 'closed negatively' verdict (deuteron_wall_full_transseries_probe) rests on the WRONG transform applied to the WRONG object (qou-hok7). That probe resummed a_D^(n)=I(n)/n — the q=1 CLASSICAL telephone period — with the CLASSICAL level-1/2 Borel divisor Γ(n/2+1). But lever1_transfer_operator_spectral_qgevrey (PR-landed) measured the SUBSTRATE object Z_n(q₀) to be q-Gevrey (log Z_n is Theta(n^2), order ~q0^{n^2/2}), strictly faster than every classical Gevrey-s (the C1 ∞-solution shares the deg_q(c_n)=n² signature). A Borel transform must divide by the growth it tames: for q-Gevrey growth q₀^{n²/2}, the classical Γ-divisor DIVERGES (q₀^{n²/2}/Γ(n/2+1)→∞, shown n≤40) while a q-Borel divisor q₀^{n²/2} tames it (=O(1)). So the classical level-1/2 Borel–Laplace is the resummation of the q=1 shadow, not the substrate object; the ~40× undershoot is a wrong-transform artifact. The deuteron-wall resummation hypothesis is NOT closed — the correct q-Borel–Laplace resummation of Z_n(q₀) (divisor q₀^{n²/2}) has not been done. Does NOT claim q-Borel reaches B_D; only that the negative closure is mis-scoped and must be redone with q-Borel. scope-(a) mis-scope, not exclusion; no fit; nothing wired.

data.verdict: deuteron-wall resummation REOPENED: closed on wrong object+transform
